mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days. This effect is consistent across monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS decline in the next 5 days is associated with negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in unemployment rate above 0.2 percentage points over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises >0.2pp in 3 months, 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts and retail sales indicates strong consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through increased corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS rise, 5-day returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL>3.0%), 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production signals weakening manufacturing activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate profits face headwinds.
failure_condition: INDPRO decline is associated with positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates robust residential construction activity, which is a leading indicator of strong consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST growth is associated with negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate during a monetary easing cycle compresses equity discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS decline in the next 60 days is associated with negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong labor market growth, measured by payroll employment exceeding 0.5% monthly, signals robust economic activity and consumer spending, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth >0.5% leads to negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases.
